title: God's Own Country: Munnar Hills, Periyar & Backwaters
tagline: Wake up to misty emerald tea plantations, cruise calm backwater lagoons, and breathe fragrant spice groves.

bestTime.notes: October through March offers cool misty hill weather and sunny, tranquil backwater cruising; monsoon (June-August) provides traditional Ayurvedic rejuvenation.

visaInfo: Domestic destination: Indian travellers require a valid government photo ID card (Aadhaar, Passport, or Voter ID). Foreign travellers require an Indian Visa/e-Visa and passport.
overview: Immerse your senses in the verdant paradise of Kerala on this handcrafted seven-day journey across the Western Ghats and palm-sheltered Arabian backwaters. Begin amidst the colonial history of Fort Kochi, watching cantilevered Chinese fishing nets dip into the sunset tide. Journey upward through winding cloud-kissed mountain roads to Munnar, where endless rolling carpeted tea hills stretch toward Anamudi peak. Track the endangered Nilgiri Tahr along the cliff paths of Eravikulam National Park and savor fresh single-estate brew at the historic Tata Tea Museum. Wind through cardamom, cinnamon, and pepper hills to Thekkady for an aromatic spice plantation walk and live Kalaripayattu martial arts display. The journey reaches its serene zenith as you step onto your private traditional thatch-roofed Kettuvallam houseboat in Alleppey, gliding along Vembanad Lake canals while feasting on fresh Karimeen fish and Malabar curries. Complete with verified chauffeur transfers, boutique nature resorts, and daily breakfasts, this is Kerala at its most enchanting.

Scenic drive through the Western Ghats with photo stops at Cheeyappara Waterfalls

itinerary.title: Arrival in Cochin & Fort Kochi Colonial Heritage
itinerary.description: Arrive at Cochin International Airport (COK) where your private chauffeur welcomes you. Transfer 42 kilometers across backwater bridges to your heritage hotel in historic Fort Kochi. After checking in and freshening up, take a guided afternoon stroll along the waterfront promenade. Watch the iconic 14th-century Chinese fishing nets swing into the Arabian Sea against the golden sunset. Visit St. Francis Church, the oldest European church in India where Vasco da Gama was initially buried, and browse antique curiosities along Jew Street.
itinerary.transferInfo: Private AC vehicle transfer from Cochin Airport to Fort Kochi (42 km, 1 hr 15 mins).

itinerary.title: Cochin to Munnar via Cheeyappara & Valara Waterfalls
itinerary.description: After a hearty South Indian breakfast, depart Cochin for the four-hour ascent into the misty Western Ghats heading toward Munnar. Watch the coastal plains give way to cascading rubber estates, pineapple groves, and deep forested mountain ravines. En route, pause at the tiered Cheeyappara Waterfalls tumbling down seven rocky tiers, followed by the lush gorge of Valara Falls. Arrive at Munnar (5,200 ft) by early afternoon. Check into your mountain resort perched above misty tea valleys and spend the evening enjoying crisp mountain breezes.
itinerary.transferInfo: Private vehicle drive from Cochin to Munnar (130 km, 4 hours via NH85 with waterfall stops).

itinerary.title: Munnar Tea Plantations, Eravikulam & Mattupetty Dam
itinerary.description: Wake to morning mist swirling across the tea valleys. Travel by department eco-bus into Eravikulam National Park, home to the largest surviving population of the endangered Nilgiri Tahr mountain goat. Hike along gentle paved trails offering sweeping views of Anamudi, South India's highest peak. In the afternoon, visit the historic Tata Tea Museum to witness century-old orthodox tea rolling machinery and sample fresh golden Pekoe. Continue to scenic Mattupetty Dam and Echo Point before returning to the resort for an evening bonfire.
itinerary.transferInfo: Private AC vehicle for full-day Munnar circuit sightseeing (approx. 50 km total).

itinerary.title: Munnar to Thekkady: Spice Plantations & Cultural Evening
itinerary.description: Check out after breakfast and drive south through the Cardamom Hills to Thekkady, the spice capital of Kerala adjoining Periyar Tiger Reserve. The scenic 90-kilometer drive winds past rubber and coffee plantations. Arrive and check into your eco-lodge surrounded by towering trees. In the afternoon, embark on an aromatic guided walking tour through an organic spice plantation to touch and smell growing pepper vines, green cardamom, cinnamon bark, and nutmeg. In the evening, witness an enthralling live performance of Kalaripayattu martial arts.
itinerary.transferInfo: Private vehicle drive from Munnar to Thekkady (90 km, 3 hours via SH17).

itinerary.title: Thekkady Wildlife & Alleppey Backwaters Houseboat Cruise
itinerary.description: Take an optional early morning boat safari on Periyar Lake inside the sanctuary before descending from the hills toward the coastal backwaters of Alleppey. Arrive at the private jetty by noon and board your traditional thatch-roofed Kettuvallam houseboat. As the captain navigates into the palm-canopied canals of Vembanad Lake, savor a fresh lunch of Karimeen Pollichathu and piping hot red rice prepared by your private onboard chef. Drift past duck farming hamlets, coir-weaving village docks, and water lilies before anchoring for a tranquil starlit dinner.
itinerary.transferInfo: Private vehicle drive from Thekkady to Alleppey jetty (135 km, 3.5 hours) followed by backwater cruise.

itinerary.title: Alleppey Backwaters to Cochin & Jew Town History
itinerary.description: Savor morning tea on the open sundeck as the sun rises over water lilies and village canoes glide past. Enjoy a freshly prepared breakfast of soft appams and vegetable stew before disembarking at 9:30 AM. Drive 55 kilometers north along the coastal highway to Cochin. Check into your luxury city hotel. Spend the afternoon exploring Mattancherry Palace with its exquisite 16th-century Hindu mythological murals, followed by the Paradesi Jewish Synagogue with its hand-painted blue Cantonese porcelain tiles and historic clock tower.
itinerary.transferInfo: Private AC vehicle from Alleppey to Cochin (55 km, 1.5 hours) and afternoon city tour.

itinerary.title: Lulu Mall Souvenirs & Airport Departure
itinerary.description: Enjoy a relaxed breakfast at your hotel. Spend your morning picking up authentic banana chips fried in pure coconut oil, Kasavu handloom sarees, aromatic tea packs, and Malabar spices at Cochin's vibrant markets or the grand Lulu Mall. Return to the hotel for checkout. Your chauffeur will provide a punctual transfer to Cochin International Airport (COK) or Ernakulam Railway Station for your onward journey, leaving you deeply rejuvenated by the beauty and warmth of God's Own Country.
itinerary.transferInfo: Private AC sedan transfer from hotel to Cochin Airport (COK) (28 km, 45 mins).

tips: Eravikulam National Park remains closed annually for approximately 4-6 weeks during the Nilgiri Tahr calving season (usually February to March); during this time, an alternate tea estate viewpoint is provided.
Houseboat air conditioning operates strictly from 9:00 PM to 6:00 AM on Deluxe category boats per local canal emission rules; Premium category houseboats feature 24-hour climate control.
Houseboats anchor at dock by 5:30 PM in accordance with Kerala Government water authority rules to allow night fishing nets to be laid out safely.
Carry modest attire when visiting temples and the Jewish Synagogue; footwear must be removed outside religious premises.

faqs.question: Is the Alleppey houseboat private for our family or shared?
faqs.answer: Our packages feature an exclusive, fully private houseboat for your travelling party. You will have a dedicated captain, navigator, and private chef on board catering solely to your preferences.

faqs.question: What is the food like on board the houseboat?
faqs.answer: Meals are freshly prepared on board using local ingredients. Typical lunch includes traditional Kerala rice, sambar, thoran, avial, and freshly caught Karimeen fish fry. Vegetarian, Jain, and North Indian meal choices are gladly accommodated on request.

faqs.question: How cold does it get in Munnar?
faqs.answer: Munnar sits at an altitude of 5,200 feet. Daytime temperatures range from 18°C to 24°C, while nighttime temperatures can dip to 10°C to 14°C between November and February. A light fleece jacket or shawl is recommended.

faqs.question: Can elderly travellers and young children comfortably do this circuit?
faqs.answer: Yes. This circuit is one of India's most popular family routes with well-paved highways, gentle walks, and relaxing boat experiences. Vehicles stop at scenic viewpoints to break up hill driving.

faqs.question: Are vegetarian and Jain food easily available in Kerala?
faqs.answer: Yes, Kerala boasts one of India's richest vegetarian culinary traditions with dishes like Sadya, vegetable stew with appams, and dosas. All partner hotels and the houseboat chef gladly prepare pure vegetarian and Jain meals without onion or garlic upon prior notice.

faqs.question: What spices are best to buy in Thekkady?
faqs.answer: Thekkady is world-famous for fresh green cardamom, Tellicherry black peppercorns, whole cinnamon bark, cloves, nutmeg, and organic vanilla pods. We take you to authorized cooperative government-approved spice gardens.

faqs.question: What is Kalaripayattu?
faqs.answer: Kalaripayattu is one of the oldest fighting martial arts systems on earth, originating in Kerala over 3,000 years ago. The live 1-hour evening performance showcases incredible agility, flexibility, sword duels, and fire acrobatics.
